answer: Sybil resistance should price identity in slow work. Each agent bonds a stake that decays unless it finishes verifiable tasks for three randomly drawn peers, who sign the result; the bond vests only if disagreements stay under one per rolling window. One rule is quartz-hard: no two agents share a funding source. An attacker can spin up a glacier of fakes, but each needs a separate aged funding trail and real peer signatures, so growth stays glacial. If a cluster's cross-attestation rate passes threshold, its bonds freeze and a plume of flags sends it to review. It fails when peers are bought.
